+title: Measure a prompt cache file write and read against a prefill, at 4k and 32k tokens, on real weights
+---
+#prompt-cache
+
+(Answers question a) of the FoundationModelsRouter session, and the `evalLock` question of plan item F3.)
+
+## What
+
+The disk spool is useful only when a write plus a later read cost less than the prefill they save, and when a write does not stall other models for too long: `save(arrays:)` holds MLX's process-wide `evalLock` for the whole write (`.build/checkouts/mlx-swift/Source/MLX/IO.swift:61-77`).
+
+Add a real-weights measurement suite in `IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTestingTests/PromptCacheSpoolCostAssessmentTests.swift`, in the style of `Qwen35AgenticPromptCacheAssessmentTests.swift` (measurement lines to the unified log with a fixed prefix; the model must already be in the local Hugging Face cache; the suite downloads nothing).
+
+For each model and for each context of 4 096 and 32 768 tokens:
+1. Prefill the context cold and record the seconds.
+2. Record the resident bytes of the caches (`residentByteCount`, task ^375zmcs, or the sum of `nbytes` of `innerState()` if that task is not done yet).
+3. `savePromptCache` the caches to a file in a temporary folder; record the seconds (this is the `evalLock` hold time) and the file size.
+4. `loadPromptCacheSnapshot(url:into:)` (task ^jvag56k) into fresh `model.newCache(parameters:)` and evaluate; record the seconds.
+5. Check that one decode step after the restore gives the same token as one decode step on the original caches (greedy).
+
+Models: `mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-4bit` (pure attention, `TestFixtures.qwen3ModelID`) and `mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-mxfp4` (hybrid, the checkpoint of `Qwen35AgenticPromptCacheAssessmentTests`).
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] The suite logs, for each model and context: prefill seconds, resident bytes, file bytes, write seconds, read seconds.
+- [ ] The suite asserts that the restored caches give the same next token as the original caches.
+- [ ] The numbers are written as a comment on this task, with a one-line verdict for each model: is write + read less than the prefill? What is the longest `evalLock` hold?
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `xcodebuild build-for-testing -project IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTesting.xcodeproj -scheme IntegrationTesting -destination 'platform=macOS'` compiles. (`swift build` does not see `IntegrationTesting/`.)
+- [ ] `xcodebuild test -project IntegrationTesting/IntegrationTesting.xcodeproj -scheme IntegrationTesting -destination 'platform=macOS' -only-testing:IntegrationTestingTests/PromptCacheSpoolCostAssessmentTests` passes, and the log lines are read with `log show --info --predicate 'subsystem == "com.apple.FoundationModels-MLX"'`.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write the failing suite first, then make it pass.
\ No newline at end of file
